name: Toyota Highlander
engine: 3.5L naturally-aspirated V6 (2GR-FKS), 295 hp — 2.5L hybrid, 243 hp combined (2020–2022; the 2023 refresh replaced the V6 with a 2.4L turbo I4)
fuel_economy: 21 city / 29 hwy mpg (FWD V6) · 20 / 27 (AWD V6) · 36 combined (hybrid)
reliability: 8/10 — the XU70 Highlander pairs Toyota's long-proven 3.5L V6 (2020–2022) or its efficient four-cylinder hybrid with a well-sorted 8-speed automatic, and it earns a strong dependability record as a three-row family SUV. There is little unusual to watch beyond the industry-wide 2020 Denso fuel-pump recall and the usual gripes about a tight third row and firm ride on big wheels. The hybrid, in particular, is a standout for a three-row, returning around 35 mpg.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate · Maintenance ~$500/yr · Strong resale — three-row Toyotas hold value well · The hybrid's ~35 mpg is remarkable for the size and makes it the running-cost pick
popular_mods: All-weather floor liners and a cargo liner for the third-row/trunk area — essential for family and dog duty
Roof crossbars plus a cargo box, and a trailer hitch (V6 tows up to ~5,000 lbs)
A second set of wheels with dedicated winter tires for the AWD
Sunshades and rear-seat organizers for family duty
Honest take: the Highlander is a family hauler — money is better spent on the hybrid powertrain, good tires, and protection than on power
oil_type: 0W-16 full synthetic (V6 uses 0W-20 — check the cap)

generations.3rd Gen XU50 (2014–2019 US): The roomy, value three-row — 3.5L V6 with a 6- then 8-speed automatic, plus a V6 hybrid. Comfortable and famously durable.
generations.4th Gen XU70 (2020–present US): A TNGA-K redesign — 295 hp V6 (2020–2022) or a 243 hp four-cylinder hybrid, 8-speed automatic, available AWD, and standard Toyota Safety Sense. The 2023 refresh dropped the V6 for a 265 hp 2.4L turbo four.
generations.Grand Highlander (2024+): A larger, genuinely three-row-friendly companion model for families who found the Highlander's back row tight.

common_issues: 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall — industry-wide; confirm it is closed by VIN
A tight third row and modest cargo space behind it — the common family complaint about this generation
Firmer ride and more road noise on the larger-wheeled Limited/Platinum trims
Infotainment on early XU70 cars felt dated; later years improved it
The 2023+ 2.4L turbo four trades some smoothness for efficiency versus the outgoing V6 — a character change, not a fault
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the specified synthetic oil on the Maintenance Minder
Service the 8-speed automatic fluid on schedule despite 'lifetime' claims
Confirm the fuel-pump recall and any open recalls by VIN
On the hybrid, keep the traction-battery cooling intake clear and the 12V battery healthy
Budget for brakes and tires given the vehicle's weight; otherwise upkeep is routine
